facts.statement: Unasuchus is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodyliforms belonging to the family Hylaeochampsidae.
facts.quote: Unasuchus is an extinct genus of Early Cretaceous eusuchian belonging to the family Hylaeochampsidae.

facts.statement: The genus name Unasuchus honors the municipality of Uña in central Spain, where the fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: The genus is named after Uña, a municipality in central Spain where fossils have been found.

facts.statement: Fossils of Unasuchus consist only of skull and jaw fragments.
facts.quote: Unasuchus is known only from skull and jaw fragments

facts.statement: The type species, Unasuchus reginae, was formally named in 1992.
facts.quote: the type species, U. reginae, was named in 1992.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis suggests that Unasuchus is a derived member of the family Hylaeochampsidae.
facts.quote: the cladistic analysis of Turcosuchus recovers Unasuchus as a derived hylaeochampsid.

facts.statement: Unasuchus lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
Fossils of Unasuchus have been found in the Barremian Las Hoyas Formation.
facts.quote: These remains have been found from the Barremian Las Hoyas Formation.

facts.statement: The genus Unasuchus existed from the Hauterivian to the Barremian, between 132.6 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Barremian (132.6 to 121.4 million years ago)
